speaker: Abu Noor
text: So. Ten at night, and I was still in Baghdad.

speaker: Guest, then Abu Noor
text: And then you died? / No. That is not how it went.

speaker: Child, then Abu Noor
text: Then how are you HERE? / ...Good question. Again.

speaker: Driver
text: Fourth gear! Tell them about fourth gear!

speaker: Uncle
text: All night? At your age? In that car?

speaker: Aunt
text: Drink your tea before it goes cold.

speaker: Old woman
text: God keep you, my son. Not so fast.

speaker: Old woman
text: Eat, my son. A thin man should not drive at night.

speaker: Old woman
text: Give it here. Straight. Like this.

speaker: Old woman
text: O Protector. O Protector. O Protector.

speaker: Soldier
text: Wake me at the checkpoint. Not before.

speaker: Soldier
text: Take one. They are the army's.

speaker: Soldier
text: What? I am awake. I was awake.

speaker: Drummer
text: Mind the drum. It is worth more than the car.

speaker: Student
text: Basra? I can pay. A little.

speaker: Student
text: I have it. He says ten, for the airport.

speaker: Boy
text: My master says a car like this should not still be running.

speaker: Boy
text: I have the wheel. Three seconds.

speaker: Boy
text: Don't touch the lever. I am in there.

speaker: Newsreader
text: Traffic police are out on the southern road tonight.

speaker: Noor, then Abu Noor
text: They say one hand doesn't clap. / No. But it drives.
Blessed: the next scrape lights no lamp
(his phone rings in his pocket: Noor)
The street: %s m to the bay
In the bay: turn the key
Checkpoint: the soldier is %s s away
